Looking at the recent trend in the Morning Consult tracker, I see a general decline from the mid-44s in July to the low 42s by late August, followed by some stabilization around 41-42% in September (41.04 → 41.73 → 41.94).

Key contextual factors:
- The NBC News poll (Sep 20) shows Trump at 41% among registered voters, described as a "second-term low"
- Negative economic news: inflation accelerating, gas prices spiking, diesel at record highs
- A Morning Consult wave from Sep 4-6 showed 43% approval, but the tracker's house-effect-adjusted average runs lower
- The Republican National Convention (Sep 9-10) may have provided a small bump, but economic headwinds likely offset it
- Other pollsters (Quinnipiac 33%, YouGov 37%, Reuters 35% among adults) show lower numbers, but Morning Consult's registered-voter base runs higher

The recent stabilization around 41.5-42% suggests the next release will likely be in a similar range, with slight downward pressure from negative economic news but potential offset from convention effects.
